title: Junta Jet Bombs Monastery During Buddhist Lent Retreat in Myaung Township, Killing at Least 14
detail: At approximately 9:30am on August 21, 2026, a junta fighter jet — reportedly launched from Tada-U Airbase — dropped at least two bombs roughly 15 minutes apart on the monastery compound in Swel Le Oh Village, Myaung Township, Sagaing Region, about 75km west of Mandalay. The bombs struck the prayer hall directly, killing at least 14 people including three women and the monastery's abbot, and injuring around 20 more; some reports put the toll at 12 killed and note it could still rise given critical injuries. More than 100 people were present for a weeklong Buddhist Lent meditation retreat that had begun August 19. Five nearby homes were also destroyed. The Myanmar Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the military only targets 'terrorists' and exercises 'maximum restraint to avoid civilian harm.' Myaung Township is a resistance stronghold where the junta holds little ground but conducts frequent aerial bombardment.

media.caption: A junta fighter jet bombs a monastery compound during a Buddhist Lent retreat in Myaung Township, killing at least 14.

title: Junta Aircraft Bomb Ngapali and Nyaung Chaung Villages in Thandwe and Gwa Townships
detail: Overnight into August 21, 2026, the Arakan Army reported that eight junta jet fighters plus one Y-12 and one Y-8 aircraft dropped approximately 100 bombs across Ngapali town, Thandwe Township, and Nyaung Chaung Village, Gwa Township, in Rakhine State. The Ngapali strike killed 1 person and injured 14, while the Gwa strike injured 8. The claim has not yet been independently corroborated beyond the AA's own information desk; a separate BNI tally of Rakhine/Chin airstrikes for August 2-24 recorded a combined 19 killed/40 injured in Thandwe Township and 8 killed/9 wounded in Gwa Township for the month, consistent with continued heavy bombardment of the area but not confirming this specific night's toll.

sources.name: Global Arakan Network (citing AA Info Desk)

title: Junta Clears Villages for Russia-Backed Dawei Port Project as Min Aung Hlaing Courts Moscow
detail: Reuters reported on August 21, 2026 that Myanmar's military has deployed a roughly 700-strong column, per ACLED, into Tanintharyi Region's Dawei District since July, burning villages and sealing off land to forcibly clear ground for a Russia-backed special economic zone and deep-sea port. Three aid workers from the MAGGA Initiative were detained and killed on July 9 after encountering the column. Resistance fighters said the campaign is intended to secure the SEZ for Russian companies: 'They want to run this Dawei SEZ, so they want to clear the area here.' The offensive follows President Min Aung Hlaing's August 17-18 Moscow visit, where he discussed the Dawei port project with Vladimir Putin alongside energy and nuclear-reactor cooperation.

media.caption: A truck passes a sign on the road to the Dawei Special Economic Zone deep-sea port project.
